reviews.quote: The book is meticulous in its extensive documentation of various laws, significant legal cases, and the struggles fought in the context of caste.
Mitta's book stands out among them for exploring a theme that has remained understudied so far – the intersection of caste and law.
The author needs to be complimented for his painstaking and meticulous research

awards: Atta Galatta–Bangalore Literature Festival (AGBLF) Book Prize 2023 — Best Non-Fiction
notes: ISBN-13 9789357762946 (ISBN-10 9357762949); publisher Context, an imprint of Westland Books, 2023. AGBLF 2023 Best Non-Fiction win verified verbatim on the prize site (agblfprize.in). Three reviews confirmed verbatim from fetched pages (The Federal, The Quint, Outlook). The book is also widely reported to have won the Kalinga Literary Festival Non-Fiction Award and Valley of Words English Non-Fiction Award, but no primary source could be fetched to verify these, so they are excluded.

ISBN 9788178246406 (ISBN-10 8178246406), 432 pp. No usable press review could be verified: Scroll.in carried only a book excerpt (not a review); academic reviews exist (Amiya P. Sen, India Quarterly 79(1) 2023; Abhishek Sarkar, South Asia Research 2024) but are paywalled with no fetchable verbatim text, so reviews left empty. No award independently verified.

Metadata verified via Routledge/Springer/Goodreads: Routledge (Taylor & Francis), hardback ISBN 9781032035482, ~611 pp, published Nov 2022 (a Routledge India paperback exists, ISBN 9781032211688). reviews.quote: Though cricket remains the leitmotif, the book offers a lot more as it weaves sociopolitical events into the narrative.

notes: Metadata: HarperCollins India, published Dec 2021 (paperback ISBN 9789354892116; audiobook ISBN 9789354893261). One verbatim review verified from a fetched Gulf News page (Shabir Hussain, 17 Feb 2022). No reviews found in the preferred Indian outlets (Hindu/Scroll/Print/Frontline/Wire); HarperCollins lists jacket endorsements from Ramachandra Guha and Vir Sanghvi but these are blurbs, not press reviews, so omitted.

reviews.quote: The result is an apt introduction to the life and times of George Fernandes.
Comprehensive, evocative, and unputdownable, this definitive biography of George Fernandes is a tour de force.

notes: Full title 'The Life and Times of George Fernandes: Many Peaks of a Political Life'; Penguin Viking imprint, Penguin Random House India, published 15 Oct 2022, 624 pp; ISBN-13 9780670092888 (ISBN-10 0670092886). Two reviews verified verbatim from fetched pages (The Tribune, Borderless Journal). The Hindu and Hindustan Times also reviewed it but those domains blocked WebFetch, so their quotes are not included.
